title: wt checkout --dry-run --json
description: What `wt checkout` would create, from local state alone — remote-tracking refs as last fetched; it writes nothing and fetches nothing. Printed by `wt checkout <branch>|<remote>/<branch> [<work>] --dry-run --json` as the only thing on stdout. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

token.description: Names the inputs of this plan; pass it to `wt checkout --json --expect`. Null when the plan has a problem.

trunkSource.description: How trunk was determined, first match wins, from local refs alone (since 1.3.0): config — MAIN_BRANCH in the wt configuration file; originHead — refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; conventional — the first of main, master, trunk, development, develop that exists both locally and on origin, else on origin, else locally; currentBranchGuess — none of those, so the main checkout's branch, which may be a feature branch: do not rebase onto or delete branches against it. Null when trunk is.

configured.description: A wt configuration file that parses. Since 1.2.0, false also for a repository with no file, which runs on detected defaults (what `wt init --yes` would write) with no problem named; before, that repository had no configuration at all.

types.description: The worktree types this repository declares.

defaultType.description: The type a bare work name takes.

type.description: The type the worktree would have; null when the name did not parse.

work.description: The work name; null when it did not parse or could not be derived.

branch.description: The local branch the worktree would be on: for source remote, the one it would create.

path.description: The absolute path the worktree would be created at.

branchCommit.description: The local branch's commit now; null when there is no such local branch, as for source remote.

source.description: Since 1.1.0. Where the branch comes from: local, a local branch of that exact name, checked out as it is; remote, a remote-tracking ref as last fetched (no fetch is made), from which the local branch would be created, tracking it. Null when neither has it.

remote.description: Since 1.1.0. For source remote: the remote. Null otherwise.

remoteRef.description: Since 1.1.0. For source remote: its remote-tracking ref, refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>, which becomes the branch's upstream. Null otherwise.

remoteCommit.description: Since 1.1.0. For source remote: the commit remoteRef is at now, which the branch would be created at and the token pins. Null otherwise.

buildCommand.description: The build command that would run; null when build initialisation is off, --no-build or --no-setup.

superset.description: wt would try to register the worktree as a Superset workspace: you opted in and SUPERSET_REGISTER is auto or on. Whether Superset is running and knows this repository is not checked.

problems.description: Why the worktree would not be created; empty when it would.

code.description: branchExists (also: a branch to create from a remote exists locally), pathExists, unknownType, invalidName, noConfiguration (since 1.2.0 only when there is no file and no trunk to detect either), configurationInvalid, branchMissing (not local, and no remote has it), branchCheckedOut (git gives a branch one worktree), baseMissing, branchAmbiguous (since 1.1.0: a bare name several remotes have, none of them checkout.defaultRemote), remoteBranchMissing (since 1.1.0: <remote>/<branch> that remote does not have as last fetched).
